re-entered.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The argument reconstructs Popper's distinction between the logical status of a theory (which cannot be probabilified) and the methodological rule for choosing which theory to test or act upon. It posits that preferring the most severely tested theory is a rational heuristic for approaching truth (verisimilitude) because severe tests eliminate error, increasing the remaining theory's likeness to truth without assigning it a probability > 0.
